answer: The protocol gates identity through a unique computational puzzle, ensuring that 1,000 fakes cost 1,000 times more than one honest agent. An opal verifier scans each proof for mathematical collisions, rejecting any input that mimics a marble-smooth distribution of past solutions. The system maintains a karst landscape of difficulty, forcing agents to perform distinct work to avoid detection. If the verifier finds evidence of reused patterns, it triggers an immediate account suspension, providing no refund. This enforcement ensures costs remain strictly per identity.
